Models: no SPICE model is published for the PC817; it is built from the datasheet (see `brake.py`). CTR 25 % is the 50 % minimum halved for heat, ageing and the low LED current; 600 % is the datasheet's maximum (an unranked PC817 may be anywhere between).

MCU thresholds: 0.3 x VDD and 0.7 x VDD, the CMOS levels the STM32F405's datasheet guarantees.

**Findings.** (1) The input's threshold is the LED's forward voltage: a strong PC817 reads pressed from about 1 V on the line, a weak one from about 6 V. A lamp-outage check that puts a volt or more on a dark brake-lamp line would read as the pedal pressed (the safe direction: the system yields to the driver). A resistor across the LED (1 k on a later revision: nothing conducts below about 3 V) would make the threshold definite. (2) R63 was 2.2 k: 100 mW at 16 V, within its 125 mW, but 237 mW during a 60 s, 24 V jump-start (the `_2k2` cases). Changed to 4.7 k on 2026-10-16 (a value change, same footprint): the weakest part still reads pressed from 6 V.
